scope: Isolated actual sealed pot writer, blind candidate selection, opening, ranking and merge reader

test.provenance: Local shared-tree run; tested file untracked at execution and native worktreeDirty=true. Later commit does not upgrade provenance.

typecheck.scope: Named-file diagnostics only; whole-project cleanliness is not claimed

findings: The real writer stores empty title/text plus sealed content and blind terms. Search output matches a separate canonical transaction and opening for each returned field.
Foreign-pot and negated-term candidates are absent; matching output carries positive native tsRank.
An in-place update preserves entity identity, changes the stored tuple revision, and appears on the next reader call. An old-title oracle replay is stale; it is not an enforcement bypass.

A newly committed eligible sealed match appears in the bounded complete controlled corpus; replacing both fields with nonmatching content removes it. This establishes only that controlled candidate scenario.
After DEK rotation, both old and new envelope versions remain readable. Destroying the fixture organization's key makes the reader fail closed with OrganizationKeyUnavailableError.
limits: Provider/candidate revisions are absent, so all field oracles remain unknown/degrade; canonical xmin proves only stored tuple identity.
Synthetic provider imports and test KMS do not establish production provider currentness or production key custody.
The direct reader receives an admin client and explicit pot context; host authentication, server-owned presence, RLS and full authority/runtime closure are unmeasured.
Positive tsRank and matching candidates do not establish a captured native lexical trace or exhaustive candidate coverage.
Sealed organization and live legs, remaining field population, enforcement bypass/fix-revert, quality labels, retrieval costs, budgets, independent acceptance and shipment remain open.

launchCorrection.outcome: Failed reporter-sink preflight before Postgres allocation or test execution; managed shell did not inherit DATABASE_URL. Native shell supplied the explicit reporter-only sink for edition b.
